base-100.$description: -------------------------------------------------------------------- * Base surfaces * * Taken from the DHCW greys rather than the NHS Identity greys. DHCW * ships `$nhsw-colour-background-grey: #F0F4F5` and * `$nhsw-colour-border-grey: #D8DDE0`, both a shade cooler and lighter * than NHS Pale Grey #E8EDEE. The difference is small in isolation but * visible when a DHCW-styled panel sits next to an England-styled one, * and matching the published value is what makes a Wales service look * like a Wales service. * * These greys carry more weight on a practitioner surface than a * patient one, because they are what separates a zebra-striped worklist * row from its neighbour. #F0F4F5 against #FFFFFF is a deliberately * quiet 1.05:1 — enough to track a row across a wide table, not enough * to read as a state change. Do not darken it to "make rows clearer"; * that is what --lily-surface-sunken and a real selected-row treatment * are for. * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */ /* #FFFFFF — pure white, NHS Identity primary surface (`$nhsw-colour-background-white`)

base-200.$description: #F0F4F5 — DHCW background grey (`$nhsw-colour-background-grey`) — card backs, panel fills, alternating table rows

base-300.$description: #D8DDE0 — DHCW border grey (`$nhsw-colour-border-grey`) — borders, dividers, table rules, hover surfaces

base-content.$description: #212B32 — DHCW text primary (`$nhsw-colour-text-primary`). Note this is the NHS service-manual near-black, not NHS Black #231F20: it has a slight blue cast that sits better against the cool greys above. 14.4:1 on white — AAA.

primary.$description: -------------------------------------------------------------------- * Primary — DHCW Navy (#1B365D) * * `$nhsw-colour-button-primary` and `$nhsw-colour-text-blue` in the * NHSW component library. This is the colour of the thing you click on * a DHCW page, and it is *not* NHS Blue. * * The choice is defensible on contrast grounds alone. NHS Blue on white * is 6.4:1 — fine for large text, short of AAA for a button label at * body size. Navy is 12.1:1, which clears AAA at any size. NHS England * solved the same problem by going green; DHCW went dark. * * On a practitioner shell the navy also does real work as chrome: a * dark header band separates the application frame from the clinical * content beneath it, which an NHS Blue band does less convincingly. * ------------------------------------------------------------------

secondary.$description: -------------------------------------------------------------------- * Secondary — NHS Blue (#005EB8 / Pantone 300) * * Demoted from primary, but not diminished. Research cited in the NHS * Identity Guidelines reports that 87% of UK adults spontaneously * associate "blue and white" with the NHS, and the GIG Cymru lozenge is * the same NHS Blue as the NHS England lozenge. DHCW keeps it for the * site header band (`$nhsw-colour-site-header-background`) and for * links (`$nhsw-colour-link`). * * Used for: links, brand chrome, hovered primary surfaces. * ------------------------------------------------------------------

accent.$description: -------------------------------------------------------------------- * Accent — DHCW Gold (#AA8630) * * `$nhsw-colour-border-gold`. The only hue DHCW introduces that is not * in the NHS Identity palette, which makes it the genuine Wales * signature. In the published library it rails the inset-text component * and tops the mobile bottom-nav bar — both times as a *border*, never * as a fill or a text colour. * * This theme honours that constraint rather than generalising the * colour. Gold is 3.4:1 on white: legal as a non-text graphical * boundary, illegal as body copy. --color-accent-content is set to NHS * Black so that any component which does fill with the accent at least * pairs it with the darkest available text (4.2:1 — AA large only), and * the components that would otherwise put small text on gold are * redirected to --lily-accent-deep below. * ------------------------------------------------------------------

neutral.$description: -------------------------------------------------------------------- * Neutral — DHCW text secondary (#4C6272) * * `$nhsw-colour-text-secondary` and `$nhsw-colour-border-secondary` — * DHCW uses one slate for both muted text and strong borders, which is * why the secondary button in the published library is a white fill * with a #4C6272 border and a #4C6272 shadow. * * Used for: muted UI chrome, secondary nav, breadcrumb separators, * secondary-button borders, input borders, table rules. 6.4:1 on white * — AA body, AAA large. Do not use it for body copy at small sizes, * which on this variant means: do not use it for worklist cell text. * ------------------------------------------------------------------

info.$description: -------------------------------------------------------------------- * Info — NHS Bright Blue (#0072CE / Pantone 285) * * Retained from the NHS Identity rather than taken from DHCW, because * DHCW has no distinct info colour: its notification banner reuses the * link blue #005EB8, which this theme has already spent on * --color-secondary. Giving info its own brighter blue keeps an info * banner distinguishable from a link-coloured header band on the same * page — a distinction DHCW's own preview pages struggle to make. * ------------------------------------------------------------------

success.$description: -------------------------------------------------------------------- * Success — DHCW notification success (#00703C) * * `$nhsw-colour-notification-success`. Darker than NHS Green #009639 * (which this theme previously used), and that is the point: NHS Green * with white text is roughly 3.3:1, which fails AA for the banner * labels it was being asked to carry. #00703C is 6.2:1 with white. * * Used for: confirmation banners, saved-record states, in-range * result flags. * ------------------------------------------------------------------

warning.$description: -------------------------------------------------------------------- * Warning — DHCW warning yellow (#FACC15) * * `$nhsw-colour-warning-callout-heading`. A cooler, more lemon yellow * than NHS Warm Yellow #FFB81C, and noticeably brighter. DHCW pairs it * with a very pale #FEF9C3 panel fill rather than tinting the panel * with the heading colour, which is why --lily-warning-surface is * declared separately below instead of being mixed from this token. * * Content colour is DHCW text-primary, never white: yellow this bright * cannot carry white text at any size. * ------------------------------------------------------------------

error.$description: -------------------------------------------------------------------- * Error — DHCW delete red (#D5281B) * * `$nhsw-colour-button-delete`, also the DHCW invalid-input colour. It * sits a half-step darker than NHS Emergency Services Red #DA291C * (Pantone 485), which this theme previously used, and buys a real * accessibility improvement: 5.1:1 with white rather than 4.6:1. * * The Welsh resonance survives the swap. Pantone 485 is the red of Y * Ddraig Goch on the national flag, and #D5281B is within a couple of * ΔE of it — close enough that no one reads the destructive button as * a different red, far enough that the label is legible. * * Used for: error summaries, destructive-action buttons, validation * messages, invalid input borders, out-of-range result flags. * ------------------------------------------------------------------

focus-ring.$description: -------------------------------------------------------------------- * DHCW supporting colours * * Values the published NHSW library needs that have no slot in the * upstream `--color-*` contract. They are declared here rather than * inline in the component rules so a consumer can retheme a DHCW * service by overriding tokens alone. * * Note these are colour tokens only — none of them carries spacing. * The practitioner density scale set further down is untouched by this * block, and the component rules that consume these colours below use * the tight scale, not the patient one. * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */ /* #FFEB3B — `$nhsw-colour-focus`. The GDS-lineage focus block.

focus-text.$description: #0B0C0C — `$nhsw-colour-focus-text`. The bar under a focused link, and the text colour inside a focus block. 16.0:1 on the yellow.

accent-deep.$description: #554318 — `$nhsw-colour-shadow-exceptional-button`. The dark gold. Stands in for --color-accent anywhere small text must sit on the accent, because bright gold cannot carry text. 9.5:1 with white.

accent-soft.$description: #F5BB66 — `$nhsw-colour-button-exceptional-light`. DHCW's "exceptional" button: a warm gold fill with dark text, used for the one action on a page that is neither primary nor destructive but still must be found. 8.4:1 with text-primary.

warning-surface.$description: #FEF9C3 — `$nhsw-colour-warning-callout-background`. The pale panel behind a warning callout. Kept separate from --color-warning because DHCW does not derive one from the other.

action-green.$description: #007F3B — the DHCW action-link green. Not NHS Green: it is a shade darker so the chevron reads at 5.1:1 on white.

link-hover.$description: #003087 — `$nhsw-colour-link-hover`, NHS Dark Blue / Pantone 287. No longer the secondary token, but still the hovered link. 11.9:1.

support-aqua.$description: #00A499 — NHS Aqua Green / Pantone 3272. Demoted from the accent slot but retained: DHCW ships an `aqua-green` tag tone, and Public Health Wales and the Welsh Ambulance Service both use aqua in print. 3.1:1 on white — decorative fills and chart series only.

page-width.$description: 960px — `$nhsw-page-width`. Declared for parity with the patient variant and with DHCW, but a practitioner shell is expected to override it: a worklist or results grid wants the full viewport, not a 60rem reading column. Set --lily-page-width: none on those routes. It is a token here precisely so you can.

selector.$description: -------------------------------------------------------------------- * Geometry — practitioner variant * * Practitioner workstations favour sharp, "data-grid" geometry over * the rounder, friendlier corners on patient-facing surfaces. We * tighten every radius to 0.125rem (2px) so cells, chips, and rows * align in dense tables without the rounded-corner halo that softens * the grid. Borders stay at 1px (the NHS norm), shadows remain at 0 * (practitioner environments are often glare-prone — bedside, * theatre, A&E). * ------------------------------------------------------------------
